content.title: When is Tax Day 2026? See deadline, extension details
content.text: April 13, 2026, 10:56 a.m. ETIt's crunch time. The deadline is this week for federal and state income tax filings.Michigan residents are required to file their federal and state income taxes for 2025 by April 15, 2026, though there are exceptions for military personnel, people living out of the U.S. and for those who were impacted by a disaster, according to the Internal Revenue Service.For those who need extra time, taxpayers do have the option to request a six-month extension to avoid penalties, but "an extension of time to file is not an extension of time to pay," the IRS reminded filers.In addition, the IRS dedicates a webpage for online tools and resources to help the process.Here are the deadlines and what to know about tax extensions:When is tax day for state and federal taxes 2026?Wednesday, April 15, 2026 is the tax deadline.Can I file my taxes on April 15, 2026?Yes. April 15 is the last full day to file your state and federal taxes.If you're mailing your taxes, you may need to go to a post office for a hand stamp to ensure it is postmarked by the deadline. Recent changes mean the Postal Service may not stamp mail until several days after it is received, which could mean the IRS would consider your return late even if you dropped it off on April 15.Are there penalties for not filing my taxes?Yes. Failing to file comes with a penalty of 5% of the tax due (less any tax paid on time and available credits) for each month or partial month the return is late, the IRS says. The penalty accrues up to a maximum of 25%. The IRS also charges interest on penalties.How much time do I get after I request an extension?If you won't have your taxes complete by the end of April 15, taxpayers can request an extension up to six months to avoid late fees, so the extension gives you until Oct. 15, 2025."Make sure you pay any tax you owe by the April filing date. The extension is only for filing your return," the IRS said.Extension details, according to the IRS:An extension of time to file is not an extension of time to pay.You must file Form 4868, Application for Automatic Extension of Time To File U.S. Individual Income Tax Return by the original due date of your return.You should pay any owed taxes by your original due date to avoid possible penalties.How do I file and extension?To file a tax extension, here are the steps to take by April 15, per the IRS:Make an electronic payment using Direct Pay, debit card, credit card, or digital wallet, and indicate the payment is for an extension.File a Form 4868, Application for Automatic Extension of Time to File U.S. Individual Income Tax Return, using IRS Free File, regardless of income.Mail Form 4868 PDF if filing an extension on paper. The form must be completed and postmarked by the tax deadline and mailed to the address listed in the instructions.Does Michigan allow taxpayers more time to file?Yes. the Michigan's Department of Treasury also offers ways to request more time to file a tax return, but you still must pay taxes on time.Taxpayers are directed to send a payment of your remaining taxes to Michigan's Treasury with a copy of your federal extension, and your state deadline will be extended to match your federal due date. for those who didn't request a federal extension, they are asked to file "Application for Extension of Time to File Michigan Tax Returns (Form 4) with your payment."What are the rules for military members?According to the IRS, those who have served or are serving in the Armed Forces, contingency operation or were hospitalized can request a 180-day extension to file and pay taxes. This also applies to individuals who support those in combat such as merchant marines serving aboard vessels or Red Cross personnel.Do I get a tax return extension if I live out of the US?Yes. People who reside outside of the U.S. get a two month extension to file and pay taxes which falls on June. 15, 2026. In addition, for those who were impacted by a disaster that caused extension damage such as a flood, wildfire, tornado or ice storm may request an extension part of the disaster relief.How do I make a personal online account on the IRS website?Taxpayers may create a personal online account via the IRS's website. The account allows secure access to payments, balances, tax records and more.When creating an account, the IRS uses ID.me, an online service that protects your identity and data. You will need to verify your identity either with a selfie and a photo of your government ID, or with a live video call with an ID.me agent.Contact Sarah Moore @ smoore@lsj.com
